current_constraints: Atlas nodes require stable IDs, kind, domains, cluster, coordinates, summary, explanation, level, aliases, assumptions, evidence and status.
Atlas edges currently expose only endpoints, type, statement, assumptions, status and source evidence.
Navigation deliberately treats directed edges as undirected for discovery but displays the original relation direction; a path is not a composed implication.

source_records.title: Local Clique Covering of Graphs
source_records.author: Ramin Javadi, Zeinab Maleki & Behnaz Omoomi
source_records.note: Boolean rank, all-one rectangle covers, fixed-bipartition biclique covers and their local-incidence versions. The Atlas zero-support conventions are separate local definitions. Link and paraphrase; no downstream open-content license was established in the source review.

source_records.title: Non-deterministic Communication Complexity with Few Witnesses
source_records.author: Mauricio Karchmer, Ilan Newman, Mike Saks & Avi Wigderson
source_records.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pp. 3-5; Proposition 3 and proof
source_records.note: Unrestricted rectangle-cover number, the paper's maximum-leaf-depth nondeterministic protocol convention and the nonzero-support ceiling-log formula. The Atlas zero case and superscript notation are local. Link and paraphrase; the source review found no explicit open-content license.

nodes.label: Boolean relation matrix
nodes.summary: A finite yes-or-no table representing which labeled row and column choices are related.
nodes.explanation: Choose finite nonempty labeled sets X and Y. The entry A[x,y] is 1 exactly when x is related to y. For a Boolean function f, its communication matrix is M_f[x,y]=f(x,y). The all-zero table keeps the same nonempty row and column sets.
assumptions: X and Y are finite, nonempty and labeled
Entries are exactly 0 or 1
A rectangular X-by-Y matrix is not automatically the full symmetric adjacency matrix of a graph

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed p. 2, Boolean-matrix and bipartite-adjacency paragraphs

nodes.label: Boolean rank
nodes.summary: The fewest Boolean rank-one factors whose OR-AND product reconstructs a binary matrix.
nodes.explanation: A factor index chooses one set of rows and one set of columns. Its 1-entries form a rectangle. Boolean OR combines the rectangles, so overlap on a 1-cell is allowed.
nodes.formula: r_B(A) = min { k : A[x,y] = OR_l (U[x,l] AND V[l,y]) }
assumptions: Boolean OR-AND arithmetic
Factor dimension k may be zero
The empty disjunction is defined as 0

nodes.label: 1-support rectangle cover
nodes.summary: Cover every 1-cell of a binary matrix by all-one row-by-column blocks.
nodes.explanation: A rectangle S x T selects some rows and some columns. It is usable only when every selected cell is 1. A cover reaches every 1-cell; rectangles may overlap. The subscript in rc_1 names the cell value being covered, not a one-witness restriction.
nodes.formula: rc_1(A) = minimum number of all-one rectangles covering supp_1(A)
assumptions: X and Y are finite and nonempty
Rectangles contain no zero cell
Arbitrary overlap on 1-cells is allowed
The empty family covers empty 1-support

nodes.label: Fixed-side biclique cover
nodes.summary: Cover a bipartite graph's edges by complete bipartite subgraphs that respect its fixed labeled sides.
nodes.explanation: Keep the disjoint sides X and Y fixed. A biclique with sides S subset X and T subset Y contains exactly the edges represented by the rectangle S x T in the X-by-Y biadjacency matrix.
nodes.formula: bc(G) = minimum number of bicliques covering E(G)
assumptions: Finite simple bipartite graph
Fixed labeled nonempty sides X and Y
Use the X-by-Y biadjacency matrix, not the full symmetric adjacency matrix
The empty family covers an edgeless graph

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed p. 2, biclique-cover and biadjacency paragraphs

nodes.label: Nondeterministic communication depth
nodes.summary: Worst-case accepting protocol depth under the precise Karchmer-Newman-Saks-Wigderson convention.
nodes.explanation: One party has x and the other has y. An accepting branch identifies an all-one rectangle containing (x,y). N^1_S2 is Atlas notation for the source's n(f), measured by maximum leaf depth. It is not deterministic communication complexity and gives no privacy or implementation-latency guarantee.
assumptions: Finite nonempty input sets X and Y
M_f[x,y]=f(x,y)
S2 maximum-leaf-depth protocol convention
Accept exactly the 1-inputs
The displayed all-zero totalization is an Atlas convention

evidence.locator: Sections 2.2-2.3, printed pp. 4-5; Proposition 3 and proof for nonempty 1-support

nodes.label: Local Boolean rank
nodes.summary: Minimize the largest number of selected rectangles containing any one row or column.
nodes.explanation: This changes the objective from the total number of rectangles to the heaviest row-or-column participation. It does not count how many rectangles overlap on one matrix cell.
nodes.formula: lr_B(A) = min_C max over rows and columns of rectangle incidence in C
assumptions: Unrestricted all-one rectangle covers
Incidence is measured per row or column
X and Y are nonempty so the maximum is defined
The empty cover gives load zero on empty support

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 2-3, local Boolean-rank definition

nodes.label: Local biclique cover number
nodes.summary: Minimize the largest number of selected covering bicliques containing any one vertex.
nodes.explanation: This is a vertex-load objective for a biclique edge cover. It is distinct from the total number of bicliques and from the number of witnesses covering an individual edge.
nodes.formula: lbc(G) = min_C max_v number of bicliques in C containing v
assumptions: Finite simple graph with fixed labeled nonempty bipartition
Incidence is measured per vertex
The empty cover gives every vertex load zero in an edgeless graph

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 2-3, local biclique-cover definition

relationships.statement: For the stated Boolean conventions, r_B(A)=rc_1(A).
assumptions: Finite nonempty labeled X and Y
Boolean OR-AND factors
Unrestricted overlapping all-one rectangle cover
k=0 and empty OR are allowed
relationships.source_scope: S1 supports the factor/rectangle correspondence. It does not separately supply the Atlas empty-support normalization.

witness_translation.forward: For each factor index l, take S_l={x:U[x,l]=1} and T_l={y:V[l,y]=1}. Its support S_l x T_l contains no zero of A, and the union covers every 1-cell; omit empty factors.
witness_translation.reverse: For each chosen all-one rectangle S_l x T_l, use the indicator of S_l as a factor column and the indicator of T_l as a factor row. Their Boolean OR-AND product reconstructs A.
witness_translation.result: A factorization with k factors gives a cover with at most k rectangles after empty factors are omitted, while a cover with t rectangles gives a factorization with exactly t factors. The two inequalities make the minima equal.

local_boundary_case.case: A is all-zero on the still nonempty X and Y
local_boundary_case.argument: The empty Boolean product reconstructs zero and the empty family covers empty support; nonnegative objectives make both minima zero.

notation_boundaries: rc_1 names the covered cell value and maps to S2 kappa(A)
It is not S2 kappa_1(A), which restricts each 1-cell to at most one covering rectangle

relationships.statement: For a graph with its fixed labeled bipartition, rc_1(A_G)=bc(G).
assumptions: Finite simple bipartite G
Fixed labeled nonempty sides X and Y
A_G is the X-by-Y biadjacency matrix
Bicliques respect the fixed sides
relationships.source_scope: S1 supports the rectangle/biclique correspondence. The empty-cover normalization is stated separately by the Atlas.

witness_translation.forward: An all-one rectangle S x T gives the biclique with sides S subset X and T subset Y.
witness_translation.reverse: A covering biclique with sides S subset X and T subset Y gives the all-one rectangle S x T in A_G.
witness_translation.result: Matrix cells and graph edges correspond one-to-one, preserving cover cardinality in both directions.

local_boundary_case.case: G is edgeless on the fixed nonempty sides
local_boundary_case.argument: Both empty families cover the empty target set; nonnegative cardinalities make both minima zero.

notation_boundaries: Use the rectangular biadjacency matrix A_G, not the full symmetric adjacency matrix
The bipartition is part of the data and may not be changed during translation

relationships.statement: For nonzero f, N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2 rc_1(M_f)); with the separately defined Atlas zero case, N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2(max(1,rc_1(M_f)))).
assumptions: Finite nonempty X and Y
M_f[x,y]=f(x,y)
S2 maximum-leaf-depth nondeterministic protocol convention
Accepting-side unrestricted rectangle covers
For the cited formula, f has at least one 1-input
relationships.source_scope: S2 Proposition 3 and its proof support the nonempty-1-support formula after the explicit notation mapping. The printed logarithm does not resolve rc_1=0.

witness_translation.forward: Given t>=1 covering rectangles, the first party nondeterministically names a row-compatible rectangle using ceil(log_2 t) bits and the second party checks column membership.
witness_translation.reverse: Accepting leaves of a depth-h binary protocol are all-one rectangles covering every 1-input; there are at most 2^h leaves.
witness_translation.result: The two inequalities give the ceiling-log equality for nonempty 1-support under the S2 protocol convention.

adopted_conventions: Set rc_1(M_f)=0 using the empty cover
Use a depth-zero constant-reject protocol and set N^1_S2(f)=0
local_boundary_case.argument: There are no 1-inputs to accept, so constant rejection is sound and complete; depths are nonnegative.

notation_boundaries: N^1_S2 is Atlas notation for S2 n(f)
It is not S2 n_1(f), which restricts witness multiplicity
rc_1 is S2 unrestricted kappa, not kappa_1
This is not deterministic communication complexity
N^0_S2(f):=N^1_S2(1-f) is an Atlas complement-side definition if later displayed

evidence.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pp. 3-5; Proposition 3 and proof

relationships.statement: For a graph with its fixed labeled bipartition, lr_B(A_G)=lbc(G).
assumptions: Same fixed labeled nonempty bipartition as R2
Objective is maximum rectangle incidence per row or column
Graph objective is maximum biclique incidence per vertex
Neither objective is per-cell or per-edge witness multiplicity
relationships.source_scope: S1 defines the two local-incidence objectives and states their equality. Its text does not separately supply the Atlas empty-cover convention.

witness_translation.forward: Translate every selected rectangle S x T to the corresponding fixed-side biclique. A row or column belongs to exactly the bicliques containing its corresponding graph vertex.
witness_translation.reverse: Translate each selected fixed-side biclique back to its all-one rectangle; every vertex incidence becomes the corresponding row or column incidence.
witness_translation.result: Every cover retains the same maximum incidence objective, so the minima agree.

local_boundary_case.case: A_G has empty support and G is edgeless on nonempty X and Y
adopted_conventions: Allow empty rectangle and biclique-cover families
Assign load zero to every row, column and vertex
local_boundary_case.argument: The maximum over the still nonempty index or vertex sets is defined and equals zero; nonnegative loads make it minimal.

notation_boundaries: Local means maximum participation per row, column or vertex
It is not the number of rectangles covering an individual 1-cell and is not S2 bounded witness multiplicity

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 2-3, local Boolean-rank and local biclique-cover paragraphs

supporting_navigation_edges.statement: The positions of the 1-cells determine which all-one rectangles are available and what must be covered.
assumptions: Finite nonempty labeled X and Y
A has entries in {0,1}

supporting_navigation_edges.statement: Local Boolean rank minimizes the worst row-or-column participation over the same kind of all-one rectangle covers, rather than the total number of rectangles.
assumptions: Incidence is per row or column
Arbitrary 1-cell overlap remains allowed

supporting_navigation_edges.statement: Local biclique cover number minimizes worst vertex participation over biclique edge covers, rather than the total number of bicliques.
assumptions: Fixed labeled bipartition
Incidence is per vertex

supporting_navigation_edges.statement: The X-by-Y Boolean relation or biadjacency matrix used in R2 may be rectangular; the existing network node uses a square symmetric full-graph adjacency matrix.
assumptions: For the biadjacency reading, a fixed labeled bipartition X disjoint-union Y is retained
No equality between the two matrix objects is asserted

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed p. 2, bipartite adjacency matrix
Section 2.2, L=D-A and symmetric weighted adjacency convention

supporting_navigation_edges.purpose: This exact definitional boundary connects the new records to the existing navigation component without claiming a semantic equivalence.

journeys.title: From a yes/no table to a communication certificate
journeys.description: Follow the same collection of yes-pairs through rectangles, Boolean factors, fixed-side bicliques and one precise nondeterministic communication model.

steps.prompt: Start with a public yes/no table f(x,y). Which labeled pairs are accepted?
Group accepted pairs into row-by-column blocks that contain no rejected pair.
Read each block as one Boolean factor; overlap on accepted cells is allowed.
Keep X and Y fixed and read the same blocks as complete bipartite subgraphs.

If one machine knows x and another knows y, how many bits of branch depth identify a compatible block under the S2 model? Check the all-zero convention and what this does not say about deterministic cost, privacy, latency or deployed systems.

journeys.title: From total cover size to participant load
journeys.description: Compare minimizing the number of covering objects with minimizing how many objects touch any one row, column or vertex.

steps.prompt: First count the total number of rectangles.
Now change the objective to the busiest row or column, not the busiest cell.
Translate that row-or-column load to vertex participation while keeping the bipartition fixed.

beginner_explanation: Imagine a yes/no table. A rectangle is a block of rows and columns for which every pair says yes. The same nonempty block can be read as one Boolean factor or as one complete bipartite subgraph. Translating a solution in either direction never needs more pieces, so the two best counts are equal under the listed assumptions. In the cited nondeterministic communication model, naming one of t blocks needs ceiling(log_2 t) branch bits when at least one yes-pair exists. The all-no table is handled by a separately declared Atlas convention. These are established translations, not a new discovery or a performance claim about real software.

conditional_teaching_example.recommended_placement_if_approved: A worked-example card linked from the one-support-rectangle-cover and boolean-rank stops, immediately after the explanation that Boolean OR permits overlap.
conditional_teaching_example.schema_note: The current examples validator hard-codes artifact=fixtures/frozen.json and graph fixture IDs. A non-graph example needs a safely resolved artifact field and a kind-specific fixture validator, or it should remain documentation rather than be forced into the graph fixture collection.
conditional_teaching_example.teaching_boundary: Use the audited 3x3 record only to illustrate Boolean OR versus ordinary arithmetic addition and overlap versus partition. Label it authored finite teaching material; do not use it as a practical benchmark, discovery, general proof or impact evidence.
conditional_teaching_example.certification: This design did not inspect or certify the example's computation.

recommendation.reason: The bridge is already source-reviewed and adds a useful matrix/graph/communication path. The structured edge extension is necessary so the assumptions and local zero conventions survive API, UI and navigation instead of being buried in prose.
recommendation.material_guardrail: The R1-R4 edge statements are established known mathematics under exact conventions. The practical question is an explanatory use of the S2 model, not evidence of real-system benefit, privacy, latency, deterministic complexity, benchmark performance or novelty.
